items.title: Telangana, a major poultry hub, to host 18th Poultry India Expo from November 25 to 27
points: File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL Poultry India Expo has expanded tenfold since 2007, from 3,500 sq. metres in one hall to 35,000 sq. metres across seven halls now, reflecting the rapid growth of India’s poultry industry and rising business interest.
The 18th edition of the Expo will be held at HITEX Exhibition Centre in Hyderabad from November 25 to 27.

Organised by the Indian Poultry Equipment Manufacturers’ Association (IPEMA) under Poultry India, the expo will bring together poultry farmers, equipment manufacturers, feed producers, breeders, veterinarians and technology companies.
Poultry Knowledge Day, the expo’s flagship technical conference, will be inaugurated on November 24 at HICC–Novotel.
India, the world’s second-largest egg producer, produced 149.11 billion eggs in 2024–25, according to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025.

items.title: ECI issues fresh work allocation order; brings back oversight on IT head
points: An internal order issued on July 28 by Senior DEC Maneesh Garg had removed Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar from the charge of IT and ICT and gave Dr. Khanna a free hand, enabling her to directly report to the Commission.

Following this, two Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29 regarding the working allocation order of Dr. Garg, who had been in interim charge of Administration department.
As per the current order, dated October 4, Dr. Khanna is required to route the files related to IT/ICT and Grievances/PGRS through Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma.
Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre (NIC).
In an affidavit filed in the Supreme Court the ECI had maintained that the July 28 order had never been implemented.

items.title: Broker’s Call: NLC India (Buy)
points: NLC India reported 13.3 per cent year-on-year revenue growth to ₹4,700 crore, while EBITDA declined 2.3 per cent to ₹1,360 crore.
Reported PAT increased 83.2 per cent to ₹1,320 crore, aided by a deferred tax credit of ₹987 crore.
Thermal generation for NLC increased 14 per cent to 7.07 BU.
Generation was aided by incremental generation from its recently-commissioned Ghatampur plant for which the generation stood at 1.8 BU.

The company has outlined an aggressive expansion plan, targeting mining capacity from the current 50 mtpa to 104 mtpa by 2030, thermal power capacity from 5,960 MW to 10,020 MW, and renewable energy capacity from 1,734 MW to 10,110 MW.
These capacity additions will require a substantial capex of ₹1.01 lakh crore, which is expected to drive growth in regulated equity.
NLC has 1.7 GW of solar and 50 MW of wind projects under construction.
NLC aims to expand installed capacity to 44 GW by FY47, with regulated equity expected to increase from ₹12,400 crore to ₹19,600 crore by FY30.

items.title: Woodside to cut more than 500 jobs in $400m savings drive
points: Australian energy giant Woodside is planning to cut more than 500 jobs worldwide as part of a restructuring programme aimed at delivering $400m in annual cost savings from 2028.

The workforce reduction, equivalent to more than 10% of the company’s employees at the end of 2025, forms part of a broader effort to streamline operations, reduce external spending and reshape its oil and gas portfolio.
Woodside chief executive Liz Westcott outlined the measures during the company’s Capital Markets Day in Sydney on Thursday.
The latest savings target represents a $50m increase from the $350m previously announced and will be measured against the company’s 2025 cost base.
Its Scarborough LNG project offshore Western Australia is 99% complete, with the first LNG cargo expected before the end of 2026.
The deepwater Trion oil development offshore Mexico is targeting first production in 2028, followed by the Louisiana LNG project in 2029.
Woodside expects these developments to support sales growth of more than 30% to approximately 280m barrels of oil equivalent in 2032.

items.title: Vigilance launches inspection in welfare fund boards functioning under Keralam government

Vigilance director Manoj Abraham said in a statement that the inspections, titled ‘Operation Welfare Fund,’ were progressing in 78 offices of 16 boards functioning under the State government’s Department of Labour.
According to the VACB, the complaints that it received with regard to the functioning of the welfare fund boards were of a diverse nature.
There allegedly were instances of officials misappropriating the contribution remitted by employers to the fund.

Other complaints pertained to the payment of multiple pensions to the same individual, payment of ex gratia benefits to ineligible persons, and diversion of government assistance.

points: Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said ‘vote chori (theft)’ is just the trailer and the full picture is haq-huqooq (rights) chori’.

items.title: Sebi allows mutual fund schemes to net cash market fund settlements
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has permitted mutual fund schemes to net their fund settlement obligations for outright cash market transactions, a move aimed at reducing temporary funding requirements and improving operational efficiency.
In a circular issued on Thursday, the market regulator said that mutual fund schemes will be allowed to offset eligible purchase and sale obligations within the same scheme and settlement cycle.
The rules will come into effect from 1 April 2027.
Sebi’s latest move changes the treatment of fund obligations for eligible mutual fund transactions, without altering the requirement for securities to be settled on a gross basis.
The implementation standards for the new norms will be determined by the industry body, Association of Mutual Funds in India (Amfi).

Apoorva is a Mumbai-based journalist at Mint who covers the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), tracking the pulse of India’s capital markets, regulatory developments and the people who operate within them.

Aishwarya, a friend of Umar Muqthar, the second accused, had earlier been taken into police custody for questioning but was let off.
Meanwhile, the phone of the third accused, Ananda, that was used to summon Abhiram, is yet to be found.

The police, who are questioning Aishwarya to understand the extent of her involvement in the murder, say Umar tried to throw them off the scent by deliberately leaving his phone behind at home when he went to meet Abhiram at Pangappara.

Umar is believed to have told Aishwarya to call him and while she was on the call, he left the phone behind and went to Pangappara where the first accused, a 17-year-old juvenile, and him allegedly committed the murder.

items.title: XRP Ledger Patches Bug That Threatened Token Minting Security
points: The XRP Ledger has activated a protocol amendment called fixCleanup3_4_0 to address a permission-related vulnerability that could allow accounts authorised to burn tokens to create new ones under specific circumstances.

items.title: Sebi approves net settlement of cash market trades for mutual funds
points: India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has greenlit the introduction of net settlement for mutual fund schemes, set to take effect on April 1, 2027.
This initiative is designed to streamline funding requirements and boost market efficiency.
Previously, net settlement was exclusive to foreign portfolio investors.

items.title: Navios adds $215m tanker trio to newbuild pipeline
points: Angeliki Frangou’s Navios Maritime Partners has revealed another $215.2m in tanker newbuilding acquisitions, adding a VLCC and two MR product carriers to its expanding fleet investment programme.

The New York-listed Greek owner disclosed the three-vessel package in its third-quarter results, confirming a $124m agreement for a scrubber-fitted VLCC reached in October and a $91.2m deal for two scrubber-fitted MR2s signed in September.
In August, Navios revealed three further VLCCs costing $361.5m, building on four earlier units worth $482m and lifting its commitment at the time to seven supertankers worth $843.5m.
The latest VLCC brings the investment in that series to $967.5m.
The two additional MR2s, costing $45.6m apiece, also extend Navios’ product tanker newbuilding exposure.
Its overall fleet stands at 182 vessels, including newbuildings, split between 65 bulkers, 54 containerships and 63 tankers.

Navios’ latest results also confirmed the $488m acquisition of four 10,100 teu containership newbuildings agreed in September, a transaction previously linked to South Korea’s HJ Shipbuilding & Construction.

points: The Election Commission on Thursday announced the annual Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.

The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027.
Final publication of electoral rolls will take place on January 21, 2027.
Deletion applications must undergo field verification in cases involving repeated or multiple entries.
Electoral registration officers must personally cross-check deletions exceeding two per cent of electors at a polling station or where the same objector files more than five objections.
